title: Quantum observables as Fréchet sensitivity kernels
abstract: We present a variational--adjoint interpretation of quantum mechanics in which the interaction between forward and adjoint wavefunctions defines a general sensitivity kernel of the system. This Fréchet interaction density quantifies how perturbations in the wavefunction (or system parameters) influence a chosen observable. The familiar Born probability density appears as a special case when the adjoint wavefunction is chosen as the complex conjugate of the forward wavefunction, for which the interaction density becomes real and non-negative. Within this framework, probability is a particular positive-definite form of sensitivity described by the Fréchet interaction density.   In general, the variational--adjoint interpretation also produces Fréchet sensitivity kernels associated with other quantum observables, including momentum, energy, and spin. This suggests that the Born probability density belongs to a broader class of Fréchet sensitivity kernels associated with quantum observables. The proposed interpretation also provides a connection with time-symmetric interpretations of quantum mechanics and possible future applications in quantum control and quantum metrology.
summary: This paper proposes a variational-adjoint interpretation of quantum mechanics where the interaction between forward and adjoint wavefunctions defines a general 'Fréchet sensitivity kernel.' It demonstrates that the standard Born probability rule emerges as a specific, positive-definite instance within this broader class of sensitivity measures. This offers a mathematically rigorous framework connecting quantum observables to sensitivity analysis, with implications for quantum control.
main_problem: The paper addresses the conceptual meaning of quantum mechanics by providing a variational-adjoint interpretation to reconcile the deterministic evolution of the wavefunction with the probabilistic nature of measurement outcomes.
main_result: It shows that the familiar Born probability density is a special, positive-definite case of a general 'Fréchet interaction density' derived from the interaction between forward and adjoint wavefunctions.
method: The core method is the variational-adjoint formulation applied to the Schrödinger equation, utilizing concepts from functional analysis and sensitivity analysis.
model_or_system: The system is general quantum mechanics, governed by the Schrödinger equation. The mathematical framework involves defining an adjoint wavefunction ($\psi^\dagger$) associated with a chosen observable or measurement functional.
key_observables: Fréchet interaction density, Born probability density, momentum, energy, and spin sensitivity kernels.
important_parameters: The Hamiltonian ($H$), time ($t$), and the choice of observable defining the adjoint wavefunction.
main_assumptions: The interpretation assumes the validity of a variational structure that allows the definition of an adjoint field ($\psi^\dagger$) to quantify measurement sensitivity.

why_interesting: This work provides a novel mathematical lens—sensitivity analysis—to re-examine the measurement problem in QM, potentially unifying different interpretations under a single mathematical structure.
